paper.title_en: Flavor from Consistency: Qualified-Axion, Anomaly Cancellation, and Emergent Unification
paper.abstract_en: We present a framework for flavored grand unification theory (flavored-GUT) in string-derived supergravity based on $G_{\rm SM}\times SL(2,\mathbb{Z})\times U(1)_X\times U(1)_{B-L}$, where gravity is intrinsically incorporated. We show that anomaly cancellation and Standard Model gauge coupling unification act as fundamental consistency conditions that determine the flavor structure, rather than treating flavor as an independent input. Mixed $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$, $U(1)_{X}$, $U(1)_{B-L}$, and gravitational anomalies are shown to vanish, with the anomalies induced by K{ä}hler transformations matched by those from chiral rotations of gauginos. For nontrivial $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ transformations of SM fermions, the anomaly-free conditions impose strong constraints on the quark and lepton flavor structures while leaving the strong CP phase unchanged. Quark and lepton mass hierarchies, mixing patterns, and the flavored Peccei-Quinn sector emerge from the same underlying structure. The consistency conditions fix the $U(1)_X$ breaking scale, identified with the Froggatt-Nielsen cutoff scale, thereby determining the QCD axion decay constant and predicting the axion mass $m_a=3.35\times10^{-8}$ eV, while simultaneously constraining the supersymmetry-breaking scale of ${\cal O}(10)$TeV and the seesaw scale. We show that the moduli are stabilized and that gauge-invariance-induced quantized nonperturbative indices are constrained by vacuum stability. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the fundamental consistency conditions dynamically realizes a qualified QCD axion. Our results establish a predictive framework connecting flavor physics, anomaly cancellation, SM gauge coupling unification, neutrino mass generation, gravitational dynamics, and axion physics, without invoking a conventional simple unified gauge group.
